tiles.title: The whole week on one grid.
tiles.body: Drag a shift to another person or day, copy last week, or start from a template. Hours and estimated labor cost add up as you build.
tiles.alt: The week in the schedule builder: each person's shifts by day, with hours and estimated labor cost at the top of each day.

tiles.title: Warnings, not walls.
tiles.body: Overtime, time off, double booking, short rest and short-staffed days are flagged while you build. You decide what to do.
tiles.alt: The builder's suggestions, including “Maya Torres: 48h this week, 8h overtime at 1.5×”.

tiles.title: Washington rules checked.
tiles.body: Meal breaks, rest between shifts, overtime, minors' hours and minimum wage. They're helpers, not legal advice.
tiles.alt: Washington limits for minors flagged in the builder: hours a 16- or 17-year-old may work on a school day and in a school week.

tiles.title: Today.

tiles.title: Publish, and see who hasn't looked.
tiles.body: Each person is told what changed for them, by email and phone alert. Tell everyone sends the whole schedule again.
tiles.alt: Review and publish: shifts, people, hours and labor cost, nothing urgent, and email and phone alerts ticked.
tiles.alt2: “Tell everyone”: send the whole published schedule to the team again, by email and phone alert.

proof.label: Where it started
proof.title: Spiros runs on Rotaserie.
proof.body: Rotaserie was built at Spiros, a restaurant in Shoreline, Washington, to give a busy manager her time back. It runs Spiros's schedule every week: building the week, swaps, time off and publishing to the whole team.
proof.alt: Spiro's Pizza & Pasta on Aurora Avenue in Shoreline, with a rainbow behind the sign

items.q: Do I have to type the schedule?
items.a: No. Typing is the fastest way, but you can also drag shifts on the week, tap your usual shift times, copy last week, or keep a consistent schedule that fills itself in.
No. Type to Build follows fixed rules. The one AI step is reading a photo at setup, if you choose it.

items.q: Do my staff need to download an app?
items.a: No. Rotaserie runs in any phone's browser. Staff add it to their home screen and get phone alerts like any app.
No. It was built at a restaurant, and it's ready for cafés, shops, salons, fitness studios and field crews, each with its own starting roles and shift times.
Yes. Everyone chooses English or Spanish for their own screens, emails and phone alerts.

items.q: Does it replace my point of sale or time clock?
items.a: No. Keep clocking in where you do now. Rotaserie handles the schedule, swaps, time off and messages around it, and has its own time clock if you want one.
It doesn't run payroll, process tip payouts, connect to a point-of-sale system, or track staff by GPS.

items.q: Can I get my data out?
items.a: Yes. You can download all your data whenever you like.
One price per location, with every feature included. Ask for early access and we'll walk you through it.

about.title: About Rotaserie · Built at Spiros
about.description: Rotaserie was built at Spiros, a restaurant in Shoreline, Washington, by Robert Banchero to give his mom her time back. Now it's ready to help other small businesses do the same.
about.og_description: Scheduling built at a working restaurant, to give a busy manager her time back.

a.label: About us
a.lead: Rotaserie is scheduling made by someone who grew up working the floor, for the manager who makes next week's schedule on a phone between rushes at a restaurant, café, shop, salon or studio.
a.founder_alt: The founder with three members of the Spiro's kitchen team
story: I grew up working at Spiros. I saw how much of my mom's time went into the schedule: building the week, keeping up with swaps and time-off requests, and fixing it all again when plans changed.
I wanted to give her that time back, so I built Rotaserie. Now the schedule at Spiros is built and shared from one place, and everyone has it on their phone.
Lots of small restaurants and businesses lose those same hours every week. I want to help them the way it helped my mom.

values.body: If it takes a training session, it's too complicated. Staff scan a QR code, sign in once, and they're set.
We help you get your team, roles and usual shifts in, so you're running the same day.
One price per location with everything included, and your data is always yours to take with you.
